metadata.title: Claude's Eval Skill: Audits First, Sweeps Second
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: ask Claude's eval-audit-and-sweep skill which model is cheapest and best, does it jump straight to that comparison, or does something else happen first? Lands the carry-out that the skill audits the eval before it ranks models, and only answers 'which model' when more than one model actually made the grid. Redo of the cwc-workshops Teardown skill-teardown cut; facts re-grounded directly against the source SKILL.md (the Teardown cut had added an unsourced 'grid vs. production' claim, dropped here).
metadata.anchor_pair: S03 -> S08 (must be the SAME case: the audit-before-sweep order, enforced)
metadata.one_flag: none needed - all claims restate the source SKILL.md's own text, not this reel's inference

beats.narration_text: A newcomer might expect Claude's eval skill to jump straight into sweeping models for the best one. It doesn't — it audits the eval first. So what does audit-and-sweep actually do?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types the naive claim, hesitates on 'sweeps', corrects to 'audits', lands the real question

props.text:
Claude's eval skill picks my best model — it just sweeps?
What does it actually do first?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md. Text/params match the verified-working precedent (cwc-workshops--claude-liam-edgartools-sec-data): charMs 45, hesitateBetween 10, mistakeRate 4, short text. VERIFY media/B00.mp4 by pulling a frame near the end of the beat's actual_duration_s and confirming the 'audits' replacement AND the second line are both fully typed before compiling further (BrutalistHesitantWriter's raw render is a fixed ~20s regardless of props; remotion_scenes.py must trim it to actual_duration_s).

beats.narration_text: You want to know which Claude model gives you the best results for the least cost, and you reach for a skill built for exactly that: eval-audit-and-sweep.

shot.new_visual_element: A request, and a folder that answers it

production_viz.label: A request, and a folder that answers it
production_viz.mechanic: A speech-bubble request ('cheapest model that still passes?') on the left. An arrow to a folder icon labelled eval-audit-and-sweep on the right.

beats.narration_text: The natural read: hand it your eval, ask which model wins, and it runs straight into the sweep — model versus model, cost versus quality, done.

production_viz.label: The straight-to-sweep reading
production_viz.mechanic: The folder icon glows and an arrow shoots directly to a grid labelled 'SWEEP' — skipping past a dimmed, unlabelled first box. Sell the reading as reasonable.

beats.narration_text: Hold onto the order the skill actually enforces: audit first, sweep second. Ambiguous request or not, that order doesn't move.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — audit, then sweep, in that order

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — audit, then sweep, in that order
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Two stacked boxes in serif on cream: '1. AUDIT' with a teal check, then a locked arrow down to '2. SWEEP', greyed until the first check lands. A closing line: 'ORDER DOESN'T MOVE.' THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT S08.

beats.narration_text: Ask it to skip straight to the sweep, and it won't — a sweep run over a broken eval produces misleading numbers, so audit goes first.

production_viz.label: The shortcut, blocked
production_viz.mechanic: The S02 direct arrow to SWEEP is struck through in crimson. Beneath it, a broken-eval icon (cracked golden-set card) feeds into a grid whose numbers visibly scramble — 'MISLEADING NUMBERS' in crimson.

beats.narration_text: There's no runnable script inside. Claude reads your actual eval code, reads the audit and sweep reference files, and writes the glue code your specific setup needs.

shot.new_visual_element: No script inside — just files to read

production_viz.label: No script inside — just files to read
production_viz.mechanic: A folder opens to reveal three file cards side by side — audit.md, sweep.md, tau2-bench.md — with a struck-through gear icon labelled 'NO SCRIPT'. An arrow from the files toward a hand-drawn 'glue code' card.

beats.narration_text: First it locates your eval — the golden set, the scoring function, the one command that runs a full pass.

shot.new_visual_element: Locating the eval: three parts found

production_viz.label: Locating the eval: three parts found
production_viz.mechanic: A magnifying glass sweeps across a codebase outline and highlights three cards in turn: GOLDEN SET, SCORING FUNCTION, RUN-ONE-PASS COMMAND — each checked teal as it's found.

beats.narration_text: The audit is a health check: task design, harness design, metric hygiene, and whether the grader itself is biased.

production_viz.label: The audit checklist, four items
production_viz.mechanic: A clipboard with four items ticking down in teal: TASK DESIGN, HARNESS DESIGN, METRIC HYGIENE, GRADER BIAS. A small stethoscope-style cross icon marks it as a health check.

beats.narration_text: Only once the audit clears does the sweep run — the full grid, every accessible model against every parameter setting, never trimmed down early.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — audit clears, sweep unlocks

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — audit clears, sweep unlocks
production_viz.mechanic: THE S03 TWO-BOX COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical. '1. AUDIT' checks teal, the lock on '2. SWEEP' springs open, and it expands into a full grid of model-x-parameter cells filling in left to right, uncut.

beats.narration_text: With two or more models cleared for access, the grid genuinely answers which model wins — cost against quality, side by side.

production_viz.label: Two-plus models: a real answer
production_viz.mechanic: Three model columns in the grid, each with a cost-vs-quality point plotted. One point rises above the rest, teal ring around it, stamp 'WHICH MODEL WINS'.

beats.narration_text: It flips the moment only one model survives that access check — now the grid can only rank that model's own settings, not the field.

shot.new_visual_element: Mirroring S09: one model, settings only

production_viz.label: Mirroring S09: one model, settings only
production_viz.mechanic: Mirroring S09's layout: two of the three model columns fade to grey and drop away, leaving one column whose rows are parameter settings instead of models. Crimson stamp 'SETTINGS, NOT THE FIELD'.

beats.narration_text: Eval-audit-and-sweep audits the eval before it ranks models — and it only answers "which model" when more than one model actually made the grid.

props.quote: Eval-audit-and-sweep audits the eval before it ranks models — and it only answers "which model" when more than one model actually made the grid.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me: "Read the eval-audit-and-sweep skill, and tell me: if I ask you to find my cheapest model that still passes, what do you check before you ever run the sweep, and why?" Liam, in for Bear.
